speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have had increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific trauma, such as a fall or twist, that might have caused this? Additionally, does the pain worsen with activity or at night while resting?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) or early-onset Rheumatoid Arthritis. The chronic nature (2 months), severe night pain awakening the patient, and lack of relief with NSAIDs in a 24-year-old male are concerning for an inflammatory etiology rather than a simple mechanical injury. I will now request inflammatory markers and imaging to confirm. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP. REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Knee_Xray, Left_Knee_MRI.
